mainTopic: Liability for different kinds of עבודה זרה: one חטאת or many, a קרבן for speech alone, and which acts get lashes
overview: The amud opens with רבי אמי, who says that someone who sacrificed, burned incense, and poured a libation to an idol in one lapse of awareness brings only one חטאת. אביי explains this from ״לא תעבדם״, but the גמרא shows that אביי himself holds the acts are divided, based on the three mentions of השתחואה. The גמרא then reworks אביי's reading of those three verses. Next, רב rules that saying ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ to an idol obligates a person who did it by mistake to bring a קרבן. The גמרא explains that this follows רבי עקיבא, and the עגל פסוק links speech to real worship. That פסוק leads to an אגדה about the plural ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״, where אחרים and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי disagree. Finally, the גמרא asks which lesser acts toward an idol get lashes. רב דימי's report of רבי אלעזר falls because those acts come from a לאו שבכללות, so the גמרא adopts רבין's version and explains it through רבי יהודה. The amud ends as a ברייתא about leftover קרבן פסח meat begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Several acts of idol worship in one lapse bring only one offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that זיבוח, קיטור and ניסוך done to an idol in one העלם bring only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: If someone slaughtered, burned incense, and poured a libation to an idol, all during one lapse of awareness, he brings only one sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אמי about someone who did several different acts of idol worship by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, separate forbidden acts can each require their own חטאת. רבי אמי says that here, three different worship acts done in one forgetful period count as only one sin, so only one חטאת is brought.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered an animal as an offering
He burned incense or offering parts
He poured a libation (a drink offering)
One lapse of awareness: he did it all by mistake without remembering in between
Obligated to bring one sin-offering

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
If one sacrificed, burned incense, and poured a libation
phrases.notes: All three acts are done as worship to an idol.

phrases.english: in one lapse of awareness,
he is obligated to bring only one offering.
phrases.notes: He means one חטאת, the sin-offering brought for a mistaken sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Several different acts of עבודה זרה done in one העלם bring only one חטאת.

steps.title: אביי explains רבי אמי's source
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that ״לא תעבדם״ groups all forms of worship into one act.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What is רבי אמי's reason? The פסוק says 'Do not worship them', so the תורה made all the types of worship into one worship.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the source for רבי אמי's ruling from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses one general word, 'worship', that covers every way of serving an idol. Because the תורה lists them under one heading, אביי reads it as making them all one prohibition. That is why they bring only one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'Do not worship them', the general ban on serving idols
One single act of worship

phrases.english: Abaye said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Ami?
The verse says: "Nor worship them,"
phrases.notes: שמות 20:5

phrases.english: the verse made them all into one act of worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for רבי אמי's ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״לא תעבדם״ combines all forms of עבודה זרה into one prohibition.

steps.title: אביי elsewhere says each act of worship is counted separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: אביי himself taught that one of the three השתחואה verses comes 'to divide' the acts of worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does אביי really say this? But אביי said: why does the תורה mention bowing to an idol three times? One is for an idol normally worshipped by bowing, one is for an idol not normally worshipped that way, and one is to divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks step 2 by quoting a different teaching of אביי that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his other teaching, אביי uses an extra verse 'to divide', meaning each type of worship gets its own חטאת. That clashes with his explanation of רבי אמי, where all the acts count as one. So how can אביי say both?

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (a challenge formula)
But didn't he say...?
Bowing down
Its normal way of being worshipped
To divide: each act counts separately

steps.confusionAlert: 'לחלק' here does not mean dividing up idols. It means each act of worship is counted on its own for a separate חטאת, which is the opposite of רבי אמי's rule.

phrases.english: And does Abaye say this?
But didn't Abaye say:
Why are there three mentions of bowing in idol worship?
phrases.notes: The three are שמות 20:5, שמות 23:24, and שמות 34:14.

phrases.english: One is for its normal manner of worship,
and one is for when it is not its normal manner,
and one is to divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר אַבָּיֵי הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's explanation in step 2 using another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation that ״לא תעבדם״ makes all worship one act.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי elsewhere says a verse comes 'to divide' acts of idol worship, so each brings its own חטאת. This contradicts treating them as one.

steps.title: אביי was only explaining רבי אמי's view
steps.stepSummary: אביי gave רבי אמי's reasoning but does not personally agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to רבי אמי's words, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction: אביי was just explaining someone else's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Explaining a view is not the same as agreeing with it. אביי showed how רבי אמי reads the פסוק, but his own opinion is that the acts are divided, each with its own חטאת. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his words (explaining someone else's view)
He does not hold that way

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי: several worship acts in one העלם bring one חטאת, based on ״לא תעבדם״. אביי only explained this; he himself holds that each act is counted separately ('לחלק').

phrases.english: He said it according to the words of Rabbi Ami,
but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the statement only explains another Amora's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought אביי personally agreed with רבי אמי, which would contradict his own 'לחלק' teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי only explained רבי אמי's reasoning; his own view is that acts of עבודה זרה are divided, each needing a separate חטאת.

steps.title: אביי's teaching on the three bowing verses, quoted in full
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes אביי's teaching on its own: the three השתחואה verses cover bowing as the idol's normal worship, bowing when it is not its normal worship, and dividing the acts of worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the teaching itself. אביי said: why does the תורה mention bowing to an idol three times? One is for an idol that is normally worshipped by bowing. One is for an idol that is not normally worshipped by bowing. And one is to divide the acts of worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes in full the teaching of אביי that was mentioned in passing in step 3. It is setting up a question on that teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״גופא״ tells us the גמרא is returning to a statement it already cited, this time to look at it closely. אביי gives each of the three verses a separate job. The third job, ״לחלק״, is the one that clashed with רבי אמי back in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: "The matter itself". The גמרא returns to a statement it cited earlier in order to discuss it.
Bowing down. Here it means bowing to an idol.
In its normal way, meaning the idol's usual style of worship.
To divide, so that each act of worship counts as a separate sin.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Abaye said:
phrases.notes: This is the teaching of אביי that the גמרא brought up in step 3. Now it looks at it directly.

phrases.english: Why are there three mentions of bowing in connection with idol worship?
One is for an idol whose normal way of worship is bowing,
and one is for bowing when that is not its normal way,
and one is to divide.
phrases.notes: Each act of worship counts on its own and gets its own חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the teaching of אביי that was quoted in step 3 and examines it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three השתחואה verses teach: bowing as the idol's normal worship, bowing when it is not its normal worship, and that the acts of worship are divided.

steps.title: Bowing in the normal way is already known from another verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a verse is needed for bowing to an idol whose normal worship is bowing, since ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה״ already teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bowing to an idol whose normal worship is bowing? We already learn that from the verse ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first job אביי gave to the verses. That job seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה״ already makes a person liable for worshipping an idol the way its followers normally do. So a separate השתחואה verse for that case would be wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: "It comes out", meaning it is already learned from a source.
"How do these nations serve". This verse makes a person liable for worshipping an idol in its usual way.

phrases.english: For bowing as its normal way?
That is already learned from "How do these nations serve."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:30

steps.triggerLanguage: לִכְדַרְכָּהּ, מֵאֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first part of אביי's teaching in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that one השתחואה verse is for an idol normally worshipped by bowing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is already covered by ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״, so a separate verse would be extra.

steps.title: A new reading of how the three verses divide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-explains: one verse covers an idol worshipped in a respectful way similar to bowing, though not by bowing itself. One covers bowing that is nothing like its worship. One is to divide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way. One verse is for an idol whose worship is similar to bowing but is not actually bowing. One is for bowing that is not like its normal way at all. And one is to divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by rereading אביי's teaching so that no verse repeats ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bowing to an idol that is actually worshipped by bowing is left to ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״. The first השתחואה verse now covers an idol served with honor, like bowing, but not by bowing itself. The second covers bowing to an idol whose worship has nothing in common with bowing. The third still teaches ״לחלק״.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather". It brings in a corrected explanation.
"Like its way and not like its way". The worship is similar to bowing, since it is honorable, but bowing is not the actual way it is worshipped.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read ״אַחַת כְּדַרְכָּהּ״ here as the same case as before. It now means an idol worshipped in an honorable way similar to bowing, but not by bowing itself.
steps.whatToRemember: Bowing is forbidden to any idol. The three verses together cover worship that is similar to bowing and worship that is not, and they also teach that each act of worship counts on its own (״לחלק״).

phrases.english: Rather, one is for an idol worshipped in a way like bowing, but not by bowing,
and one is for bowing that is not like its way at all,
and one is to divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by rereading אביי's teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One verse was for an idol whose normal worship is bowing, which would repeat ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״.
steps.terutzMaskana: One verse is for worship similar to bowing but not by bowing, one is for bowing that is unlike its worship, and one is to divide.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: accepting an idol as a god
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's cases of someone who accepts an idol as a god and someone who says to it ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who accepts an idol upon himself as a god, or one who says to it, "You are my god."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting words from the משנה. It is setting up רב's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are cases where the person does no physical act of worship. He only accepts the idol, or says something to it. The question in the background is whether that alone is enough to be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: One who accepts it upon himself as a god.
"You are my god". These words are said to the idol.

phrases.english: One who accepts it upon himself as a god,
one who says to it, "You are my god."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְקַבְּלוֹ עָלָיו בֶּאֱלוֹהַּ, הָאוֹמֵר לוֹ אֵלִי אַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after the השתחואה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה counts accepting an idol as a god, or saying ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״, among the ways a person becomes liable for idol worship.

steps.title: Saying "You are my god" alone makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רבה בר אבוה, who quotes רב: as soon as a person says ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ to an idol, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: once he said to it, "You are my god," he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב rules on the משנה's case. Speaking the words is enough to make a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No act of worship is needed. Saying ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ to the idol is itself treated as idol worship, and the person is חייב as soon as he says it.

keyTerms.meaning: "Once" or "as soon as".
Liable to punishment.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that idol worship can be done through speech alone, not only through physical acts like bowing or offering.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
Once he said to it, "You are my god," he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב: כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ אֵלִי אַתָּה חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling on the משנה's case quoted in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ to an idol makes a person חייב right away, even without any act of worship.

steps.title: What kind of liability does רב mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב's word חייב means. It cannot mean the death penalty, because the משנה already says that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Liable for what? If he means liable to death, that is already stated in our משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what punishment רב had in mind when he said the person is חייב. It rules out the death penalty, which sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already lists someone who says ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ among those who are put to death. If רב were only teaching the death penalty, his statement would add nothing. So the גמרא looks for a different kind of liability.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? (Liable to what?)
Death, execution by בית דין
It is already in our משנה

phrases.english: For what?
If for the death penalty,
it is already in our משנה!
phrases.notes: This is the משנה quoted back in step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of רב's ruling from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of liability does רב's word חייב refer to?

steps.title: רב means a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רב means that someone who said ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ by mistake must bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he means liable to bring an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב was talking about a קרבן, not the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה covers someone who did it on purpose, who gets the death penalty. רב adds a new point: someone who did it without knowing it was forbidden must bring a חטאת, even though he only spoke.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering, here a חטאת for an act done by mistake

phrases.english: Rather, for an offering.
phrases.notes: This is for someone who said it by mistake. He brings a חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's חייב means a person who says it by mistake must bring a קרבן.

steps.title: The רבנן require a real action for a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: a ברייתא, as ריש לקיש explains it, shows that the רבנן require a real action before a person brings a קרבן. Speech alone is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this hold even according to the רבנן? But a ברייתא teaches: a person is liable only for something that involves an action, such as slaughtering, burning, pouring, or bowing. ריש לקיש said: Who taught bowing? It is רבי עקיבא, who says we do not require an action. This implies that the רבנן hold that we do require an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's ruling. Since the רבנן demand a real action before someone brings a קרבן, a person who only spoke should not have to bring one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists bowing as an action, and ריש לקיש says only רבי עקיבא would count something as small as bowing. So the רבנן must require a more substantial action. If bowing is not enough for them, words alone are surely not enough, and רב's ruling seems to contradict the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)
An action, a physical deed
Slaughtering, burning, pouring (acts of worship)
By implication; this shows that
We require

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume everyone counts bowing as an action. ריש לקיש says the ברייתא that lists bowing follows only רבי עקיבא. The רבנן require a real action, so for them bowing is not enough, and speech surely is not.

phrases.english: And even according to the Rabbis?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
He is not liable except
for a matter that involves an action,
such as slaughtering and burning,
and pouring and bowing.
And ריש לקיש said:
Who taught bowing?
It is רבי עקיבא,
who says we do not require an action.
phrases.notes: He means a real, substantial action. A small movement like bowing is enough for רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: This implies that the Rabbis
hold that we do require an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of step 11, that speech makes a person bring a קרבן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that saying ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ makes a person bring a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן require a real action for a קרבן. Speech is not a real action, so רב's ruling seems to go against the רבנן.

steps.title: רב follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's ruling follows רבי עקיבא, who does not require a real action.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב said it too, he said it according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying that רב holds like רבי עקיבא, not the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts that the רבנן would not require a קרבן for speech alone. It narrows רב's ruling to רבי עקיבא's opinion, where a real action is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said it
Also, too

phrases.english: When רב said it too,
he said it according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to one opinion (רבי עקיבא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב's ruling held for everyone, including the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's ruling follows only רבי עקיבא, who does not require a real action for a קרבן.

steps.title: According to רבי עקיבא it is obvious, like a מגדף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: according to רבי עקיבא, רב's ruling is obvious, since it is the same as the case of a מגדף.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא, it is obvious! This is the same as a blasphemer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: if רב follows רבי עקיבא, his ruling teaches nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא already rules that a מגדף brings a קרבן, even though he does no action and only speaks. Saying ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ is also only speech, so why would רב need to say it? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (why say it?)
That is the same as
A blasphemer, someone who curses ה׳

phrases.english: According to רבי עקיבא, it is obvious!
That is the same as a blasphemer.
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא already makes a blasphemer bring a קרבן for speech alone, so this case seems no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב's ruling follows רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא already holds that a מגדף brings a קרבן for speech alone. So רב's ruling about ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ would add nothing new.

steps.title: רב's ruling is not obvious, because the verse links speech to worship
steps.stepSummary: You might think רבי עקיבא requires a קרבן for speech only for a מגדף, where כרת is written. רב teaches that accepting an idol is compared to actual worship, so it also requires a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי עקיבא only requires a קרבן for speech in the case of a מגדף, because the Torah writes כרת for him. But here, where כרת is not written, you would say no קרבן is needed. So רב teaches us that the two are compared, as the פסוק says: 'They bowed to it, sacrificed to it, and said...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 14. It explains why רב's ruling is not obvious even according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said רב's ruling is just like the case of a מגדף. The answer is that the מגדף case is special, because the Torah clearly writes כרת for him. Saying ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ has no written כרת, so רב needed a פסוק to show it is treated like real idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: the mistaken idea the ruling comes to block
He teaches us: the real point of the ruling
Being cut off. The heavenly punishment for certain sins. A קרבן is only brought for a mistaken sin that carries כרת
They are truly compared: the Torah puts them side by side, so they share the same law

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling is needed because a מגדף has כרת written in the Torah, while saying ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״ does not. The פסוק of the עגל puts 'said' next to 'bowed' and 'sacrificed,' so they share one law.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב is disagreeing with רבי עקיבא. רב follows רבי עקיבא. He is only teaching that רבי עקיבא's rule reaches this case too.

phrases.english: Lest you say:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קׇרְבָּן
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva only obligates an offering
in the case of a blasphemer,
since karet is written about him.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is במדבר 15:30.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּלָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: But here, where karet is not written about it,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means someone who accepts an idol as his god by saying ״אֵלִי אַתָּה״.

phrases.english: I would say: no offering.
He teaches us that they are truly compared,
as it is written:
"And they bowed to it, and sacrificed to it, and said, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:8, about the עגל. 'Said' sits right next to bowing and sacrificing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it's obvious' challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is needed, because a reasonable mistaken assumption would have said otherwise.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's rule applies only to a מגדף, where כרת is written explicitly.
steps.terutzMaskana: Accepting an idol is compared by the פסוק to real worship, so a קרבן is required.

steps.title: The extra ו in ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״ saved the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that without the plural ו in ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״, the Jewish people would have deserved destruction for the עגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If not for the ו in ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״, the 'haters of Israel' would have been sentenced to destruction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the same פסוק it just quoted. It focuses on one letter in the words the people said at the עגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ו makes ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״ ('brought you up') plural. That plural form is what saved the people from being destroyed. This is a side point on the פסוק, not part of the debate about קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter ו
'Brought you up' in the plural, from 'these are your gods who brought you up from מצרים'
'The haters of Israel': a polite way of saying Israel itself
Total destruction

steps.confusionAlert: 'The haters of Israel' does not mean Israel's enemies. It is a polite way to talk about the Jewish people themselves, so we don't say something bad about them directly.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Were it not for the vav in "which brought you up,"
phrases.notes: That ו makes the word plural: 'they brought you up.'

phrases.english: the haters of Israel would have been sentenced to destruction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the פסוק quoted in Step 15 and teaches something new from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plural ו in ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״ saved the Jewish people from destruction after the עגל.

steps.title: A group of תנאים said the same thing as רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's teaching matches a view held by תנאים called אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute among the תנאים: אחרים say, if not for the ו in ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״, the 'haters of Israel' would have been sentenced to destruction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן's idea already appears among the תנאים. It quotes the view of אחרים, which uses the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כתנאי tells us this was a debated question among earlier תנאים. רבי יוחנן's view matches the side called אחרים. The other side, רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, disagrees in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like the תנאים': this question was already debated by earlier sages
'Others': a name used for a certain תנא or group of תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's teaching about the ו is not new with him. It matches the view of the תנאים called אחרים.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute among the Tannaim:
Others say:
Were it not for the vav in "which brought you up,"
the haters of Israel would have been sentenced to destruction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that Step 16's teaching matches a view among the תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching about the ו in ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The view of אחרים, one side of a dispute among the תנאים.

steps.title: Joining God's name with an idol is already deadly
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי rejects the idea that mentioning God together with the idol would have saved the people. Anyone who joins God's name with an idol deserves to be uprooted anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי said to him: But anyone who joins the name of Heaven with an idol is uprooted from the world, as the verse says, "only to ה׳ alone"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי argues against אחרים, who said in the last step that the plural ו in ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״ saved the people from destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים thought that worshipping the idol alone would earn destruction, while mixing in God's name made it less severe. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says the opposite: the פסוק shows that serving anything together with God is itself a capital sin. So the ו cannot be what saved them.

keyTerms.meaning: one who joins or partners (God's name with something else)
the name of Heaven, meaning God
literally 'something else'; a polite way of saying an idol
uprooted from the world

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said to him:
But isn't anyone who joins
the name of Heaven and something else
phrases.notes: "Something else" is a polite way of saying an idol.

phrases.english: uprooted from the world,
as it says: "except to ה׳ alone"!
phrases.notes: שמות 22:19

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי: וַהֲלֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the view of אחרים quoted in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim of אחרים that the plural ו in ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״ saved the Jewish people.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Joining God's name with an idol is itself punishable by destruction, so including God could not have protected them.

steps.title: The plural means they wanted many gods
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי gives his own explanation of the plural word ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״. It shows that the people desired many gods.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, why does the verse say "who brought you up" in the plural? To teach that they desired many gods.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected אחרים, רבי שמעון בן יוחאי offers a new meaning for the plural word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אחרים, the plural was a point in the people's favor. For רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, it counts against them. It shows they were not satisfied with one idol and wanted many gods.

keyTerms.meaning: what the verse comes to teach
they desired
many gods

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, the plural ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״ does not soften the sin of the עגל. It shows the people wanted many gods.

phrases.english: Rather, what does the verse teach by saying
"who brought you up" (in the plural)?
That they desired many gods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's replacement reading after his rejection in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plural ״הֶעֱלוּךָ״ teaches that the Jewish people desired many gods.

steps.title: Lashes for the lesser acts of idol service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about hugging, kissing, sweeping, and sprinkling before an idol. רב דימי reports that רבי אלעזר says all these get lashes, except vowing or swearing in the idol's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: But one who hugs, kisses, sweeps, or sprinkles water before an idol, and so on. When רב דימי came, he said that רבי אלעזר says: For all of them he gets lashes, except one who vows in its name or confirms an oath in its name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה. These are acts toward an idol that are forbidden but do not carry the death penalty. רבי אלעזר rules that they get מלקות, with two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said these acts are forbidden. It did not say what punishment they bring. רבי אלעזר adds that they get lashes, but vowing or swearing in an idol's name does not.

keyTerms.meaning: one who hugs (an idol)
one who sweeps, and one who sprinkles water to settle the dust
gets lashes (מַלְקוּת)
one who makes a vow in the idol's name
one who confirms his words with an oath in the idol's name

phrases.english: But one who hugs or one who kisses (an idol),
one who sweeps or one who sprinkles water, etc.
When Rav Dimi came (from Eretz Yisrael),
he said that Rabbi Elazar says:
For all of them he gets lashes,
except for one who vows in its name
and one who confirms (an oath) in its name.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by returning to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the lesser acts of idol service get מלקות, except vowing or swearing in the idol's name.

steps.title: Why no lashes for vowing in its name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why vowing or swearing in an idol's name is different, so that there are no lashes for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about one who vows in its name or confirms in its name, that he does not get lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אלעזר's two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר gave lashes for most of the list but not for these two. The גמרא wants to know what makes them different. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: what is different?
he gets lashes (Aramaic)

phrases.english: What is different about one who vows in its name
and one who confirms in its name, that he does not get lashes?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הַנּוֹדֵר בִּשְׁמוֹ וְהַמְקַיֵּים בִּשְׁמוֹ דְּלָא לָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the exceptions in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why vowing or swearing in an idol's name does not get מלקות.

steps.title: Because they involve no action
steps.stepSummary: Vowing and swearing are only speech. A לאו שאין בו מעשה, a prohibition broken without an action, does not get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a prohibition that has no action in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: vowing and swearing are just words, not deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that lashes are given only for a prohibition broken through an action. Vowing and swearing are done with the mouth alone, so they are not punished with lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: a prohibition broken without any physical action

phrases.english: Because it is
a prohibition that has no action in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and such a prohibition does not get מלקות.

steps.title: The other acts are a general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: hugging, kissing, and the rest also should not get lashes. They fall under a לאו שבכללות, and no lashes are given for that kind of prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these too are a general prohibition, and we do not give lashes for a general prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the main part of רבי אלעזר's ruling, that the other acts get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition against these acts comes from one verse that covers many different acts together. That is called a לאו שבכללות. Since there are no lashes for such a prohibition, it is hard to see how רבי אלעזר can give lashes for them.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'general' prohibition: one verse that bundles several different prohibitions together
these too

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. A לאו שאין בו מעשה means no action is involved. A לאו שבכללות means one verse covers many acts. Each rule is a separate reason for no lashes.

phrases.english: These too are a general prohibition,
phrases.notes: "These" means hugging, kissing, sweeping, and sprinkling, the acts רבי אלעזר said get lashes.

phrases.english: and we do not give lashes for a general prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the main ruling of step 20 by using the idea of 'no lashes' from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that hugging, kissing, and similar acts get מלקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These acts are banned only by a לאו שבכללות, and such a prohibition does not get lashes.

steps.title: Source showing a general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about eating from an animal before it dies. It comes from the verse ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״, which is the classic example of a לאו שבכללות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As was taught in a ברייתא: From where do we know that one who eats from an animal before its soul leaves it breaks a prohibition? The verse says: "Do not eat over the blood."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the idea of a לאו שבכללות. The ברייתא continues in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״ is used to teach several different prohibitions. The first one here is eating from an animal while it is still alive. Because one verse carries many prohibitions, it serves as the model of a לאו שבכללות.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a בְּרַיְיתָא
before its soul leaves it, meaning before the animal fully dies
a negative commandment, a prohibition

phrases.english: As was taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know that one who eats from an animal
before its soul leaves it
breaks a prohibition?
The verse says: "You shall not eat over the blood."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:26. Here "blood" stands for the animal's life, which is still inside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the idea of לאו שבכללות used in the challenge of step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The idea of a לאו שבכללות, one verse holding several prohibitions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the verse ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״ (ויקרא 19:26). It continues in steps 25–28.

steps.title: Another teaching: no eating meat while the blood is still in the bowl
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a second meaning of ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״: the meat of a קרבן may not be eaten before its blood is sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another teaching from "You shall not eat with the blood": do not eat the meat while the blood is still in the bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and pulls a second, completely different law out of the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first teaching was about eating from a living animal. Now the same words teach a law about קרבנות: the meat is forbidden until the blood in the מזרק is sprinkled on the מזבח. One verse is now carrying two unrelated prohibitions, which builds the picture of a לאו שבכללות.

keyTerms.meaning: Another teaching; a second way to read the same verse
The bowl used to catch a קרבן's blood and sprinkle it
Meat

phrases.english: Another matter:
"You shall not eat with the blood"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:26

phrases.english: you shall not eat meat
while the blood is still in the bowl.
phrases.notes: This is talking about a קרבן. Its meat can't be eaten until its blood has been sprinkled on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 24 with a second law from the same verse.
steps.raayaObject: That ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״ is a לאו שבכללות that covers many separate prohibitions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's second reading of ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״: no eating קרבן meat before the blood is sprinkled.

steps.title: רבי דוסא: no mourners' meal for those executed by the court
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא learns from the same verse that the mourners' meal is not served after the burial of someone executed by the בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: How do we know that we do not serve the mourners' meal for people executed by the court? The verse says, "You shall not eat with the blood."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a third law from the same verse, this time in the name of רבי דוסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, after a burial, others give the mourners a comforting meal. רבי דוסא reads the verse as saying: do not eat this meal over the 'blood' of someone the court executed. This is a third unrelated law, all from one לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: Serving the mourners' first meal after the burial
People put to death by the court
The verse teaches; introduces the source

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
From where do we know that we do not serve the mourners' meal
phrases.notes: מברין is the meal that friends bring to mourners when they come home from the burial.

phrases.english: for those executed by the court?
The verse states:
"You shall not eat with the blood."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִין שֶׁאֵין מַבְרִין עַל הֲרוּגֵי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third law from the same verse.
steps.raayaObject: That one verse covers many prohibitions, so it is a לאו שבכללות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי דוסא's teaching on the mourners' meal.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: judges who sentence someone to death fast that whole day
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from the verse that a סנהדרין that sentenced someone to death may not eat anything for the rest of that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: How do we know that a סנהדרין that put someone to death may not taste anything that whole day? The verse says, "You shall not eat with the blood."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a fourth law from the same verse, from רבי עקיבא, about the judges themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'blood' is the life of the person the judges sentenced. On that day the judges may not eat at all. This is yet another separate law drawn from one לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: The high court that judged capital cases
Killed a person; here it means they sentenced someone to death
Taste; eat even a little

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
From where do we know about a Sanhedrin that killed a person
phrases.notes: The judges didn't kill anyone with their own hands. It means they sentenced someone to death.

phrases.english: that they may not taste anything
that entire day?
The verse states:
"You shall not eat with the blood."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לְסַנְהֶדְרִין שֶׁהָרְגוּ אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth law from the same verse.
steps.raayaObject: That ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״ includes many separate prohibitions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's teaching about judges fasting.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the warning for the בן סורר ומורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finds the Torah's warning (אזהרה) against the behavior of a בן סורר ומורה in the same verse, which ends the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: Where is the warning for a בן סורר ומורה? The verse says, "You shall not eat with the blood."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא's last teaching: רבי יוחנן uses the same verse as the warning for the בן סורר ומורה. This finishes the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah spells out the punishment of a בן סורר ומורה, but it never writes out a clear warning against what he does. רבי יוחנן reads the verse as: do not eat in a way that leads to a death penalty. Now one verse holds five separate laws. That is the clearest picture of a לאו שבכללות, and it backs up the challenge in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah's warning (a לאו) that forbids an action
The stubborn and rebellious son
One prohibition that covers many different laws; no lashes are given for it

steps.whatToRemember: ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״ teaches at least five different laws. Because one לאו covers so many things, it is the standard example of a לאו שבכללות, and no lashes are given for breaking it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't get distracted by the details of each law. The גמרא brought this ברייתא for one reason: to show that one verse covering many prohibitions is a לאו שבכללות. That is the challenge against רבי אלעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the model the גמרא uses to show why a broad prohibition like the one on hugging and kissing an idol might not get lashes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
From where is the warning for a stubborn and rebellious son?
The verse states:
"You shall not eat with the blood."
phrases.notes: Read here as: don't eat in a way that ends in a death penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַזְהָרָה לְבֵן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fifth and final law from the verse and closes the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״ is a לאו שבכללות, which supports the challenge against רבי אלעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching on the warning for a בן סורר ומורה, ending the ברייתא.

steps.title: No lashes for anything learned from a general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין בר חייא (some say רבי אבין בר כהנא) rules that none of the lessons from ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״ carry lashes, because the verse is a לאו שבכללות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין בר חייא said (some say it was רבי אבין בר כהנא): for all of these, a person does not get lashes, because the verse is a general prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the ברייתא's list, an אמורא says that none of the prohibitions learned from this one verse are punished with lashes. This completes the proof for the challenge in step 23 against רב דימי's report of רבי אלעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לאו שבכללות is one negative command that covers several different acts. The rule is that you do not get lashes for breaking it. So any prohibition that only comes from such a verse cannot carry lashes, and the earlier version of רבי אלעזר's ruling can no longer stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A general prohibition: one negative command that includes several different forbidden acts
Gets lashes (מלקות) as a punishment
"And some say": a second version of who said the statement

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not just a new fact. It is used here to knock down the earlier report of רבי אלעזר's view, which is why the גמרא's next word is אלא, "rather."

phrases.english: And Rabbi Avin bar Ḥiyya said,
and some say it was Rabbi Avin bar Kahana:
For all of them, one is not flogged,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means every lesson the ברייתא just learned from ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״.

phrases.english: because it is a general prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof for step 23's challenge: after the ברייתא shows one verse holds many prohibitions, רבי אבין rules that none of them get lashes. This brings down רב דימי's version of רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier report that רבי אלעזר holds one gets lashes for these idol-worship acts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Those acts are learned from a verse that is a לאו שבכללות, and no lashes are given for a לאו שבכללות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No lashes for any prohibition learned from ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַל הַדָּם״, since it is a לאו שבכללות.

steps.title: רבין's different version of רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: Because of the challenge, the גמרא turns to רבין's report: רבי אלעזר said there are no lashes for any of the items in the משנה, except vowing in an idol's name and confirming an oath in its name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי אלעזר: for all of them a person does not get lashes, except for one who vows in its name and one who confirms an oath in its name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier version of רבי אלעזר and replaces it with רבין's version. In this version most of the משנה's items get no lashes, with two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the earlier report is being thrown out. In רבין's version, רבי אלעזר agrees there are no lashes for the actions learned from the general verse. Lashes remain only for vowing and swearing in an idol's name.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל) and reported a teaching
One who makes a vow in the name of an idol
One who confirms his words with an oath in an idol's name

phrases.english: Rather, when Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Elazar said:
For all of them, one is not flogged,
phrases.notes: Here "all of them" means the list of forbidden acts in our משנה.

phrases.english: except for one who vows in its name
and one who affirms an oath in its name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to Step 29 by replacing the challenged version of רבי אלעזר's view with רבין's version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the report of what the אמורא actually said
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר gives lashes for the idol-worship actions, such as hugging and kissing.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר gives no lashes for those actions, only for vowing or swearing in an idol's name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No lashes for the משנה's items, except vowing and swearing in an idol's name.

steps.title: But vowing and swearing involve no action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why only vowing and swearing in an idol's name get lashes. They are a לאו שאין בו מעשה, and that normally means no lashes either.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about those for which one does not get lashes? They are a general prohibition. But these too are a prohibition that has no action!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבין's version. The two exceptions should also have no lashes, because they are only speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other items avoid lashes because they come from a לאו שבכללות. Vowing and swearing have a different problem: nothing physical is done. Normally a לאו שאין בו מעשה does not carry lashes, so the exceptions seem to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is different?": asks for the reason behind a distinction
A prohibition broken without any physical action, such as by speech alone
"These too": points out that the same problem applies to the other cases

phrases.english: What is different about those for which one is not flogged?
That they are a general prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי נָמֵי לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה נִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: These too are a prohibition that does not involve an action!
phrases.notes: "These" means vowing and swearing in the idol's name. They are just words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the two exceptions in רבין's version from Step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exceptions of vowing and swearing in רבין's version of רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These acts involve no physical action, and a לאו שאין בו מעשה should not carry lashes.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר's ruling follows רבי יהודה, who holds that one does get lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ruling follows רבי יהודה, who says: for a prohibition with no action, one does get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by tying רבי אלעזר's ruling to רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that a לאו שאין בו מעשה never brings lashes. רבי יהודה disagrees and gives lashes even for such a prohibition. Under his view, vowing and swearing in an idol's name can get lashes, and רבין's version holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: "That one": here, רבי אלעזר's ruling
One gets lashes for it

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: no lashes for the idol-worship actions learned from the general verse (a לאו שבכללות). There are lashes for vowing or swearing in an idol's name, following רבי יהודה, who gives lashes even for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a ruling can depend on an earlier מחלוקת: the exceptions work only under רבי יהודה's view about prohibitions that involve no action.

phrases.english: That one is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who says:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה – לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: A prohibition that does not involve an action, one is flogged for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the ruling to a תנא's opinion (רבי יהודה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No lashes are ever given for a לאו שאין בו מעשה, so the exceptions make no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר follows רבי יהודה, who gives lashes even for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.

steps.title: A ברייתא on leftover קרבן פסח meat begins the proof about רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to quote a ברייתא showing that רבי יהודה gives lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה. The ברייתא opens with the פסוק ״לֹא תוֹתִירוּ מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר״ and says the תורה gives a positive command, an עשה, after the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "You shall not leave any of it until morning." The verse comes to give a positive command after a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up its last answer by bringing a ברייתא as a source for רבי יהודה's view. This line only begins the ברייתא, so it sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two parts: "do not leave any over" (a לא תעשה), and "what is left over, burn in fire" (an עשה). The ברייתא says the burning command comes after the prohibition, so it is the way to fix the broken prohibition. Leaving meat over means not doing anything, so it is a classic case of a לאו שאין בו מעשה. That is why this ברייתא can show what רבי יהודה holds.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches. This introduces a source from the time of the תנאים.
Do not leave over. This is the prohibition on keeping meat of the קרבן פסח until morning.
A positive commandment, something the Torah tells you to do.
A prohibition, something the Torah tells you not to do.
The verse comes to teach. It explains the purpose of a פסוק.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think of 'leaving over' as an action. The person simply did nothing with the meat. That is exactly why this case fits the topic of a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source that will show רבי יהודה's view on lashes. That view is what makes sense of רבי אלעזר's ruling that vowing and swearing in an idol's name carry lashes.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"You shall not leave any of it until morning"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:10, about the meat of the קרבן פסח. The rest of the פסוק says to burn whatever is left over.

phrases.english: The verse comes to give
a positive command after a prohibition,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support Step 32's claim that רבי יהודה gives lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds one gets lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ״לֹא תוֹתִירוּ מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר״ (שמות 12:10), explaining that the Torah gives an עשה after the לא תעשה.
